title: Quantum Approximate Optimization via Noise-Directed Adaptive Warm-Starting
authors: Filip B. Maciejewski, Stuart Hadfield, Oscar Wallis, George Pennington, Sebastian Brandhofer, Stefan Woerner, Daniel J. Egger, Davide Venturelli
abstract: Progress towards a quantum advantage using known heuristic methods for combinatorial optimization is impeded by hardware noise and limited qubit count. Here, we propose a noise-aware adaptive approach to quantum approximate optimization, Noise-Directed Adaptive Warm-Starting (ND-AWS), that builds on recent concepts such as Warm-Start QAOA and Noise-Directed Adaptive Remapping. By leveraging bitflip gauge transformations, our algorithm exploits amplitude-damping-like noise components. We experimentally implement high-performance quantum optimization ansätze on 100-qubit Ising Hamiltonians, showing that ND-AWS generally improves the performance over a non-gauge-transformed iterative Warm-Starting variant, at no additional circuit cost. This places our results among the highest-quality demonstrations of quantum optimization with similar ansätze at this scale. Crucially, the simplicity of the framework opens the door for future enhancements such as adaptive bias schedules, and integration with classical solvers.
summary: This paper introduces Noise-Directed Adaptive Warm-Starting (ND-AWS), a novel algorithm designed to boost performance in quantum optimization algorithms like QAOA when running on noisy hardware. By adaptively incorporating noise structure through gauge transformations, ND-AWS guides the search process more effectively than standard methods. The results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance for complex combinatorial problems on large superconducting quantum processors.
main_problem: The primary challenge is improving quantum approximate optimization for combinatorial problems, which is severely limited by hardware noise and restricted qubit counts.
main_result: The proposed Noise-Directed Adaptive Warm-Starting (ND-AWS) method generally improves performance over standard warm-starting techniques on 100-qubit Ising Hamiltonians without increasing circuit depth.
method: The approach combines iterative warm-starting with noise-aware gauge transformations, allowing the optimization ansatz to adaptively bias itself towards regions corresponding to high-quality solutions found in previous iterations.
model_or_system: The work is applied to solving combinatorial optimization problems encoded by a cost Hamiltonian $H_C = \sum J_{ij} Z_i Z_j$, tested experimentally on 100-qubit Ising Hamiltonians using superconducting quantum processors.
key_observables: Approximation Ratio (AR), and the distance to the optimal solution ($1-AR$).
important_parameters: Bias parameter $c$, noise strength ($q$), and the number of qubits ($\sim 100$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that hardware noise can be constructively exploited via bitflip gauge transformations to guide the optimization process towards the ideal ground state.
figures_summary: Figures compare $1-AR$ across different methods (Standard IWS vs. ND-AWS) and show how classical post-processing (HDQS) improves results, while other figures detail the iterative circuit structure and bias evolution.
paper_structure: The paper introduces ND-AWS by building upon Warm-Start QAOA and Noise-Directed Adaptive Remapping; it details the gauge transformation mechanism for hardware implementation on Ising Hamiltonians; performance is evaluated across various random graph types, comparing results with and without classical post-processing enhancements.
why_interesting: While focused on optimization, the core technique of using noise structure (amplitude damping) to guide quantum state preparation via gauge transformations is highly relevant to understanding error mitigation and variational ansatz design in open quantum systems.
